questions.prompt: What does the timestamp stored in a ShimCache entry actually represent?
options: The time the program was executed
The file's $STANDARD_INFORMATION last-modified time -- describing the file, not the run
The time the entry was written to the registry
questions.explanation: This is the most common ShimCache misreading. The stored value is the file's modified time and inherits every weakness of $SI timestamps, including susceptibility to timestomping.

questions.prompt: Why does ShimCache prove presence rather than execution on modern Windows?
options: It only records files that failed to launch
Windows 10 and later lack a reliable execution flag, and entries can be created when the shim engine examines a file for reasons other than execution, including folder browsing
questions.explanation: Older versions carried an insertion flag indicating execution; modern versions do not, so an entry establishes that the file was present and examined, nothing stronger.

questions.prompt: Why might a ShimCache entry for recent activity be missing from a live system's registry?
options: The registry value is capped at 64 entries
The cache is maintained in kernel memory and only flushed to the registry at shutdown, so recent entries exist only in memory until the host reboots
ShimCache is disabled by default on workstations
Live systems never write ShimCache data
questions.explanation: On a machine running since before the activity of interest, the relevant entries are still in memory -- which makes memory analysis the only route to them prior to a reboot.

questions.prompt: Why is an entry's position in the ShimCache list itself useful evidence?
options: Position determines whether the file executed
Entries are ordered most-recent-first, so position establishes relative recency even where timestamps are unreliable or manipulated
Position corresponds to the drive letter
questions.explanation: Since the stored timestamp describes the file rather than the event, the ordering provides an independent recency signal that timestomping does not affect.
